groups.title: the checker: reads a quest's acceptance criteria and a submission, prints PASS/FAIL per criterion, exits 1 if any fails

checks.why: tests/test_checker.py runs check() on quests/summary.json with a passing and a failing submission

risks.text: an unknown criterion type falls into `else: ok = False`, so a typo in a quest file ("max_char" for "max_chars") fails every submission under the criterion's own description, with no hint that the type was not recognised

`value` is read with c.get("value"), but every known type uses it: a criterion without value raises TypeError (`None in str`, `len(...) <= None`) and the CLI crashes with a traceback instead of printing FAIL. `type` and `description` are read with [] and raise KeyError when missing

the CLI reads the submission with open(...).read(), which keeps the file's trailing newline, and max_chars/min_chars count it: a tagline of exactly 60 characters saved by an editor that adds a final newline is 61 and fails "At most 60 characters". check() itself counts exactly what it is given

both files are opened without encoding=, so the platform default decides how they are read: on Windows a UTF-8 submission with non-ASCII text can raise UnicodeDecodeError or decode to a different character count than on Linux

groups.title: quest definitions: a title and a list of acceptance criteria, each with type, value and description

checks.why: only quests/summary.json is exercised; quests/tagline.json is not loaded by any test

risks.text: the checker knows only contains, max_chars and min_chars; any other type in a quest file always fails (see the checker group)
contains is case-sensitive and matches anywhere: "Source:" passes on "No Source: given" and fails on "source: example"

groups.title: pytest tests for check(): one passing and one failing submission for the summary quest

risks.text: nothing covers min_chars, the tagline quest, an unknown type, a missing value, or the CLI (its exit code and newline handling), so a change there passes the suite unchecked
the tests put the repository root on sys.path and import checker directly, so moving or renaming checker.py breaks the import, not an assertion
README documents the CLI as `python checker.py <quest> <submission>`; changing the argument order or the exit code changes the documented usage

rules.rule: every quest has at least one acceptance criterion, and every criterion uses a type checker.py knows (contains, max_chars, min_chars) with a value and a description
rules.why: the README promises every quest has a checkable criterion; an unknown type or a missing value is not an error at load time, it fails every submission or crashes the CLI

rules.rule: a new criterion type is added to check() and to tests/test_checker.py in the same change, with one passing and one failing case
rules.why: check() raises nothing for an unknown type, so a type that is only half wired up looks like a failing submission, not a bug

rules.rule: the CLI exits 0 only when every criterion passes and 1 otherwise
rules.why: anything scripting the checker (CI, a grader) reads the exit code, not the PASS/FAIL lines
